# Core illegal-move routine: explain a rejected move with a reason toast

**Headline:** The shared illegal-move feedback routine in `core/src/ui/` must
render the player-facing rejection reason as a transient toast, so every game
that reuses the helper explains refusals instead of only shaking the card.

## Goal

As an engine maintainer, I want the core illegal-move routine to accept a
reason string and display it as a transient toast — independently of the shake
branch — so every game built on the core explains rejected moves consistently
without writing its own overlay.

## Problem statement

`shakeIllegalMove` (`core/src/ui/shakeIllegalMove.ts`) today plays
`sfx-illegal-move`, tints and shakes the target, and drops everything else. The
rules layer already produces a player-facing sentence for every illegality
(`LegalityResult.reason`), and the game's in-game help promises that a rejected
move is "rejected with the reason" — a promise no engine or game code currently
keeps. The shake and the sound are also the only feedback for players with
reduced motion or audio off, which is an accessibility gap.

The engine half is tracked by this item; the game-side wiring and the submodule
pointer bump are tracked by **RISE-0MVPAAWIV003CE3D** in the
`tce-the-rising` store.

## Users

- **The player** — needs to know *why* a move was refused ("which card blocks
  it, or which figure I could never have met") so they can pick a legal slot.
- **The player with reduced motion / no audio** — today only gets a shake and a
  sound; the toast is the explanation channel.
- **Game developers using the core engine** — want consistent illegal-move
  feedback (shake, sound, explanation) from one entry point.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — The core routine renders the reason.** The shared illegal-move feedback helper in `core/src/ui/` accepts an optional `reason` and, when present, renders a transient toast containing that exact text. With no reason the current behaviour (tint + shake + `sfx-illegal-move`) is unchanged for existing consumers — the parameter is optional and adding it does not alter other games.
- **AC2 — Toast behaviour.** It is non-blocking (never swallows pointer input intended for cards, slots or buttons), appears above the board/overlays at a depth taken from `core/src/ui/constants.ts`, auto-dismisses after a configurable dwell (~2.5 s default), can be dismissed early, and is ephemeral (not persisted, not part of undo/redo or the transcript).
- **AC3 — Shown on every feedback branch, reduced motion included.** The toast is rendered by the core routine independently of the shake branch, so it appears when the target is a tintable `Image`/`Sprite`, when it is a non-tintable `Container`, and when reduced motion (`core/src/ui/ReducedMotion.ts` / `prefers-reduced-motion`) suppresses the shake entirely. Under reduced motion the toast still appears unobscured and is readable for its full dwell with no slide/fade animation; the existing shake-suppression behaviour is unaffected.
- **AC4 — Repeat rejects replace, never stack.** A second rejection inside the dwell window replaces the current text (and restarts the timer) instead of stacking duplicates; the toast is destroyed on scene shutdown so it cannot leak across scenes.
- **AC5 — Exported from the shared UI surface.** The helper and its option type are exported from `core/src/ui/index.ts` alongside `shakeIllegalMove` / `ShakeIllegalMoveOptions`, documented in the core UI module docs, and used by `DragDropManager`'s `onIllegal` hook where a reason is available.
- **AC6 — Tests and build green (core).** Unit coverage for the toast's text/timing model (extracted pure where practical) and for the routine's branches (no reason, reason, container target, reduced motion, replace, shutdown); `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate pass in the core repository.
- **AC7 — Documentation.** `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (component table) and `core/docs/ui/` module docs document the new option, the dwell default, the depth constants and the reduced-motion behaviour; the source JSDoc is updated.
- **AC8 — No legality change.** The rules layer is untouched: the toast only displays the reason that already existed. No new rejection paths and no re-wording of rules copy.

## Implementation slices (TDD order)

1. **Pure toast model + unit tests** — `core/src/ui/illegalMoveToast.ts`:
   framework-free model exposing `show(text)`, `dismiss()`, `tick(dt)`,
   `visible`, `remaining` and a configurable dwell (default 2500 ms);
   replace-on-show restarts the dwell. Tests in
   `core/tests/ui/illegalMoveToastModel.test.ts` written first.
2. **Routine renders the toast + tests** — add `reason?: string` and
   `dwellMs?: number` to `ShakeIllegalMoveOptions` (or a sibling
   `showIllegalMoveFeedback` that composes `shakeIllegalMove`; keep a single
   entry point and existing callers untouched). Render with `createHudText`
   (`core/src/ui/Renderer`) rather than a bespoke container — do **not** reuse
   `popTextOrIcon` for the toast itself because it destroys the text immediately
   under reduced motion. Add toast depth/colour/font constants to
   `core/src/ui/constants.ts`. Render the toast **before/independently of** the
   shake early-returns (reduced motion, null target) and for `Container`
   targets. Tests in `core/tests/ui/shakeIllegalMove.test.ts`.
3. **Drag-drop reason plumbing + tests** — carry an optional reason on
   `DragDropPayload` (or a per-registration resolver) so `onIllegal` consumers
   can display it; the default illegal feedback renders the toast when a reason
   is present; behaviour without a reason is unchanged. Tests in
   `core/tests/ui/dragDrop.test.ts`.
4. **Exports and docs** — export from `core/src/ui/index.ts`; update
   `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `core/docs/ui/`.

## Key Files

- `core/src/ui/shakeIllegalMove.ts` — the illegal-move routine; the reason
  option and toast rendering live here (or in the sibling it composes).
- `core/src/ui/illegalMoveToast.ts` — new pure text/timing model.
- `core/src/ui/index.ts` — public export surface.
- `core/src/ui/constants.ts` — toast depth/colour/typography constants.
- `core/src/ui/Renderer/index.ts` — `createHudText` text primitive to reuse.
- `core/src/ui/ReducedMotion.ts` — reduced-motion gate for the animation branch.
- `core/src/ui/dragDrop.ts` — `onIllegal` hook reason plumbing.
- `core/tests/ui/illegalMoveToastModel.test.ts`,
  `core/tests/ui/shakeIllegalMove.test.ts`,
  `core/tests/ui/dragDrop.test.ts` — unit coverage.
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `core/docs/ui/` — module docs and component table.

## Constraints

- **Repository boundary, authorised for this item.** Changes are limited to
  `core/src/ui/`, its tests and its docs.
- **Backwards compatibility.** `shakeIllegalMove` keeps its current signature
  and behaviour for every existing caller (`core/src/ui/dragDrop.ts`,
  `core/example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts`, and The Rising's
  animator); the reason is a new optional field.
- **No new dependencies** and no third toast implementation — reuse
  `createHudText` and generalise the Gym-local toast pattern
  (`core/example-games/gym/scenes/GymDlcUnlockScene.ts:365`) where practical.
- **Styling from core constants** — no hardcoded pixel positions in callers.
- **Performance.** At most one live toast object; no per-frame tweens left
  running after dismissal.
- **UK English** copy; the toast presents the rules-layer text verbatim.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Regression risk to other games (medium).** `shakeIllegalMove` is shared;
  keeping the reason optional and defaulting to no toast preserves current
  behaviour. A test pins the no-reason path.
- **Depth/input regressions (medium).** The toast must be input-transparent and
  above the board but below modal overlays and the game-over screen.
- **Copy length (low).** Rules reasons can be long; the toast must wrap and
  clamp gracefully at the design width without truncating the actionable part.
- **Assumption — verbatim reason.** The toast shows the rules-layer string
  unchanged, so rules copy changes happen in the game's ordering rules, not in
  the UI.

## Related work

- **RISE-0MVPAAWIV003CE3D** — paired game-side item (The Rising): wires the
  reason through its rejection paths, adds browser tests and bumps this repo's
  submodule pointer. Precedent pairing: RISE-0MVBUSQUR006LPVP ↔
  CG-0MVFQ6QOZ003FVO4.
- CG-0MM1OQFZE1KS6KHB — the original extraction of the illegal-move shake into
  `src/ui` (the pattern this extends).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Does this item need its own interview?** — No. The scope is fully
  specified by the paired game item's intake brief (RISE-0MVPAAWIV003CE3D, whose
  Appendix records the operator instruction and the repo research), so the
  engine ACs are lifted from that brief rather than re-litigated. Source:
  RISE-0MVPAAWIV003CE3D description and its intake comment.
- **Q: Why a separate engine item rather than all work in the game store?** —
  `core/` is the `Tableau-Card-Engine` submodule with its own worklog store; the
  cross-repo precedent (RISE-0MVBUSQUR006LPVP ↔ CG-0MVFQ6QOZ003FVO4) records
  engine authoring under a `CG-` item and the game repo bumps the pointer.

The current fix makes illegalMoveToastView itself Phaser/Renderer-value-free, restoring @ui/shakeIllegalMove and @ui/dragDrop as node-safe entry points. This follow-up records and enforces the convention:

- A documented list (docs/DEVELOPER.md, and a comment block in src/ui/index.ts or a dedicated module) of which src/ui modules are guaranteed node-safe (no Phaser value import at evaluation time) and what is required to keep them that way (type-only Phaser imports, no top-level import of Phaser-bearing modules such as ./Renderer).
- Optionally a static import-graph check that fails when a listed module transitively has a value import of 'phaser' (stronger than the evaluation-based guard; catches regressions without depending on test execution order).
- Clarify in docs that the @ui barrel is intentionally Phaser-bearing (CardGameScene extends Phaser.Scene) and that node tests must import deep Phaser-free paths rather than '@ui' itself.

Non-blocking; small task.
